title: Hunter Biden Says Father's Cancer Has Spread, Calls It 'Very Painful'
excerpt: In an emotional BBC interview, the former president's son revealed Joe Biden's prostate cancer has metastasized beyond his bones and acknowledged the presidential pardon was 'not good' for the country.
body:
• Hunter Biden told BBC Newsnight that his father's prostate cancer has metastasized beyond his bones and is causing severe pain.
  • The 83-year-old former president was diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer in May 2025 and has been undergoing radiation and hormone therapy.
  • Hunter Biden also acknowledged that Joe Biden's presidential pardon of him was 'not good' for the Constitution, the American people, or his father's legacy.
  • Despite his declining health, Joe Biden remains publicly active and plans to release a memoir, 'Promise Me, America,' on November 17.

Former President Joe Biden's prostate cancer has spread beyond his bones and is causing him significant pain, his son Hunter Biden revealed in an emotional interview with BBC Newsnight released on Friday.

"The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further," Hunter Biden, 56, told the BBC. "It's very painful and it's very debilitating in many respects."

"It's really sad to watch. The only thing that I'd say about my dad, about his health right now, is I wish he would complain more, because it's not good."

— Hunter Biden, in BBC Newsnight interview

A Diagnosis That Changed Everything

Joe Biden, 83, disclosed his cancer diagnosis in May 2025, less than four months after leaving the White House. The Biden family said at the time that the cancer was "characterized by a Gleason score of 9 (Grade Group 5) with metastasis to the bone" — one of the most aggressive forms of prostate cancer.

https://x.com/AZ_Brittney/status/2085867981821894830

While the family noted the cancer appeared to be hormone-sensitive, allowing for effective management, the disease has clearly progressed. A Biden spokesman said in October 2025 that the former president was undergoing radiation treatment and hormone therapy. A spokesman for Biden declined to comment on Hunter's latest interview, according to Reuters.

Former First Lady Jill Biden offered a candid assessment during a Today show appearance on June 1. "If he had just been diagnosed with prostate cancer, that's one thing, because that can be cured, but the fact that it metastasized to his bones, that makes it a whole different story," she said. "I think Joe will live with cancer till the rest of his life."

Hunter Biden Addresses the Pardon

The BBC interview ranged beyond health matters. Hunter Biden addressed one of the most contentious decisions of his father's presidency — the unconditional pardon issued in the final weeks of Joe Biden's term that relieved Hunter of a conviction on three felony gun charges and an upcoming sentencing hearing on nine federal tax charges.

"Was it good for our Constitution? Was it good for the American people? Was it good for my dad's legacy? No, on all counts. It was not," Hunter Biden said. "It's something that is easily criticized and for good reason. And I can't pretend otherwise."

"All I know is that I'm grateful that he did it for me. What would you have thought of my dad if he did not do that for me? And left me to the whims of Donald Trump?"

— Hunter Biden, on the presidential pardon

The pardon drew sharp bipartisan criticism at the time. Joe Biden had repeatedly stated throughout his presidency that he would not pardon his son, making the reversal a focal point for critics who accused the administration of eroding trust in the justice system. Hunter, who has publicly discussed his past struggles with alcohol and drug addiction, framed the decision as an act of fatherly protection against political adversaries in the incoming Trump administration.

Still the Center of the Family

Despite the grim health update, Hunter Biden emphasized that his father remains engaged and active. "He's still doing his thing," he said. "He so believes in this country."

Hunter described Joe Biden as the anchor of the family. "My dad is, to this day, the center of our family," he said. "He's the best father, the best husband, the best grandfather."

Biden, who was the oldest person to win the U.S. presidency at the time of his 2020 election, attended the dedication of Barack Obama's presidential library in Chicago in June. He served as Obama's vice president from 2009 to 2017.

What's Next

Joe Biden's presidential memoir, Promise Me, America, is scheduled for release on November 17. The book is expected to cover his decades in public service, including his single term as president, during which his physical health and mental acuity faced sustained scrutiny — criticism that intensified after a disastrous 2024 debate performance led to his withdrawal from the reelection race.

No further details about Biden's current treatment plan or prognosis have been released. The progression of his cancer from its initial bone metastasis to areas beyond will likely renew public attention on the health of the 83-year-old former president in the months ahead.
